iterations.narrative:
The enrichment analysis clearly points to **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism (KEGG map00590)** as the dominant affected pathway, with five of the seven input metabolites — arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, Leukotriene A4, and 15-Deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 — belonging to this pathway (FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment ≈ 1430 via the eicosanoid synthesis wrapper). A parallel enrichment for Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency further implicates the leukotriene branch. Membership verification confirms that arachidonic acid (C00219), Leukotriene A4 (C00909), and 5-HETE (C04805) are all annotated in the KEGG Arachidonic Acid Metabolism pathway.

KEGG reaction graph analysis establishes directional flow from arachidonic acid (C00219) toward both 5-HETE and Leukotriene A4 through the shared intermediate C05356 (a hydroperoxy-eicosatetraenoic acid), placing arachidonic acid definitively upstream. The presence of 15-HETE (C04742) alongside the 5-lipoxygenase product 5-HETE suggests coordinated dysregulation of both the 12-lipoxygenase and 5-lipoxygenase branches of the eicosanoid cascade. 15-Deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) represents the cyclopentenone prostaglandin arm derived from PGD2 metabolism. Losartan (C07072) is an outlier (angiotensin II receptor antagonist) and glycolaldehyde (C00266) is a glyoxal cycle intermediate, neither fitting the eicosanoid theme.

The biological significance centers on **lipid mediator storm**: elevated HETEs and Leukotriene A4 indicate heightened phospholipase A2 activity releasing arachidonic acid, followed by amplified 5-LOX and 12-LOX activity. This pattern is consistent with inflammatory activation, where eicosanoids drive leukocyte chemotaxis, vasoconstriction, and prostaglandin synthesis. 15-Deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 adds a PPARγ-activating, anti-inflammatory nuance. Together, these shifts implicate an inflammatory or hypersensitive response in the treatment group.
